row.evidence: Aircall's pricing page lists "SSO and SCIM" only on the Enterprise plan (Custom pricing, Talk to Sales); Essentials ($30) and Professional ($50) do not include them.
row.notes: Enterprise is quote-only with a 25-user minimum (Essentials/Professional: 3). SAML SSO is Enterprise-only and 'subject to certain conditions'; help centre says SAML is 'available only to a limited number of customers' and must be activated by Aircall. Aircall publishes no SCIM documentation (no endpoint, base URL or token docs found on aircall.io, developer.aircall.io or support.aircall.io), so scim_ops and idp.generic are null. The only catalogue provisioning app found is the Okta OIN 'Aircall Provisioning Connector by Aquera', built and maintained by a third party (Aquera), not Aircall; it claims create/update/deactivate/delete. Under the post-pilot rules a third-party connector does not change status, so the row records idp.okta as third_party and the status rests on the pricing page alone. Entra/Google/OneLogin/JumpCloud are documented by Aircall as custom SAML apps only. The Public REST API (users, teams, user webhooks) is on all plans per the comparison table (tier mapping read from the page's comparison-table data; icons are not quotable). Monthly billing costs more (annual = 25% discount).

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.price_text: Custom pricing (Talk to Sales), minimum 25 users

limitations.text: No public SCIM documentation: the pricing page names SCIM on Enterprise but Aircall's help centre and developer portal document no SCIM endpoint, token or attribute mapping.
The only IdP-catalogue provisioning app found is a third-party Okta connector built and maintained by Aquera, not by Aircall.

endpoints.purpose: Update a User (name, availability, role_ids, wrap-up time)
Delete a User; all associated data destroyed
Add a User to a Team
Remove a User from a Team

rate_limits.text: 120 requests per minute per company; higher limits on request via support

limitations.text: User V1 API (the only version with a documented DELETE) is announced for deprecation; User V2 documents list/get/create/update but no delete endpoint.
No deactivate/suspend operation is documented; removal is a hard delete that destroys the user's data (call recordings stay with the line).
Deleting a user frees the license for reassignment but it is still billed until removed from the contract.
List endpoints are paginated at a maximum of 50 results per page.

okta.notes: Third-party connector built and maintained by Aquera, not Aircall. The OIN page does not say whether it calls Aircall's REST API or a SCIM gateway, and none of its capability items are checked in the page markup, so kind is left null. Aircall's own Okta guide uses a custom SAML 2.0 app.

Whether SSO must be configured before SCIM is not documented.
SCIM deprovisioning behaviour (deactivate vs delete, seat release, session revocation) is undocumented.

Okta OIN page: the static HTML marks every capability with the same icon, so SSO support of the Aquera connector could not be confirmed from the catalogue (Aircall's own Okta guide uses a custom SAML 2.0 app). Whether the Aquera connector is restricted to Enterprise is not stated.
Microsoft Learn has no Aircall tutorial (aircall-tutorial and aircall-provisioning-tutorial return 404); Entra marked not listed based on Aircall's own non-gallery instruction.
